title: Projectile speed at a specified height without solving the clock first

authority_basis.claim_scope: Repository-backed SBA04 atom combines the vertical no-time relation with constant vx and total-speed reconstruction to compare speed at different heights.

concepts.statement: At a specified vertical displacement, the vertical velocity component can be related directly to height without first solving time, then combined with the unchanged horizontal component to obtain total speed.
concepts.why_required: Height-based speed questions can be solved from state relations without introducing an unnecessary clock variable.
concepts.failure_if_omitted: Learners may solve a larger time system, measure y from the wrong origin, or forget the horizontal component in total speed.

symbols.name: vertical velocity component at displacement y

conditions: y measured from the same initial state that defines u_y

symbols.name: vertical velocity component at specified height

conditions: Same state at the specified height

model_conditions.condition: Vertical motion has uniform downward gravity and horizontal acceleration is zero, with displacement y measured from the initial state used in the no-time relation.
model_conditions.physical_reason: The no-time vertical kinematic relation and constant horizontal component are model consequences of the standard projectile assumptions.
model_conditions.failure_consequence: Drag, propulsion, nonuniform gravity or origin mismatch invalidates the direct height relation.

representations.semantic_geometry: A trajectory marks the launch-height origin, apex H and another specified height y; the state at y shows unchanged ux, vertical component magnitude from the no-time relation and total speed reconstructed from components.
must_not_imply: height y is absolute rather than displacement from the declared origin
representations.verification_method: Check y uses the declared origin, evaluate vy squared from the vertical relation, retain ux, and reconstruct v squared from both components.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Declare the vertical displacement origin and identify the target height state.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: The wrong y value can be inserted even when the later algebra is correct.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Use the vertical no-time relation to determine vy squared at the target height without solving t.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: An unnecessary time variable can obscure the state relation.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Retain the constant horizontal component and combine squared components to obtain or compare total speed.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: Total speed may be replaced by vertical speed alone.

required_transformations.description: Translate a height condition into a vertical no-time component relation and then rebuild total speed using the unchanged horizontal component.
Use the height-derived squared component state to solve or compare speeds without introducing an unnecessary clock, while preserving the declared height origin and horizontal component.

misconceptions.incorrect_model: The height variable in the no-time relation can be measured from any convenient reference without changing u_y.
misconceptions.why_plausible: Diagram heights are often labeled from the ground while kinematic equations may use launch-point displacement.
misconceptions.required_counterexample: Using ground height with a launch-state u_y but launch-point kinematic origin changes the displacement and gives a different result.
misconceptions.required_representation_repair: Mark the exact y=0 state beside the trajectory before labeling the target displacement.
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: y must be the signed displacement from the same initial state that defines u_y in v_y^2=u_y^2-2gy.
misconceptions.verification: Check dimensions and substitute y=0 to recover v_y^2=u_y^2 at the initial height.

misconceptions.incorrect_model: Once vy is found at a height, its magnitude is the projectile speed.
misconceptions.why_plausible: The no-time relation solves only the vertical component and may appear to complete the problem.
misconceptions.required_counterexample: At the apex vy=0 but an oblique projectile still has nonzero horizontal speed.
misconceptions.required_representation_repair: Complete the component triangle after solving vy rather than ending at the vertical arrow.
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Use v^2=u_x^2+v_y^2 with the standard constant horizontal component.
misconceptions.verification: At apex set vy=0 and recover v=|u_x|.

problem_families.name: Projectile speed at a specified height
recognition_cues: compare speeds at heights without time
problem_families.first_technical_move: Define the vertical displacement from the correct origin and use vy squared versus y before reconstructing total speed.
fatal_errors: solve time unnecessarily and mix roots
